q: A shelter runs a tiered volunteer programme. What tasks should higher-level volunteers handle compared with lower-level volunteers?
o: Higher-level volunteers do agility, nosework, cooperative care or work with behaviourally challenged dogs, and lower-level volunteers focus on socialisation and basic cues.
Lower-level volunteers manage aggressive dogs, and higher-level volunteers walk only friendly dogs.
Both tiers do the same basic sit and down repetitions, with the higher tier doing them for longer.
e: Tiered programmes assign baseline socialisation to lower tiers and reserve advanced training, cooperative care and work with behaviourally challenged dogs for higher tiers.

q: Rehabilitating dogs with bite histories toward people or dogs needs intensive desensitisation and counter-conditioning. What success rate was documented?
o: Less than 5% of dogs were adopted successfully
87% with no subsequent bite report, with a length of stay of 1 to 3 years
100% of dogs were adopted within 2 weeks
e: Intensive rehabilitation over 1 to 3 years gave an 87% success rate, defined as adoption with no further biting.

q: A study taught randomly selected shelter dogs to approach the front of the kennel and sit when people approached. What was the adoption outcome?
o: The dogs were 1.4 times more likely to be adopted, with no effect on length of stay.
The dogs had half the length of stay, with no change in adoption rate.
The dogs were adopted at the same rate as control dogs, and their length of stay was unchanged.
e: Sit-at-the-front increased the likelihood of adoption 1.4 times but did not alter overall length of stay.

q: A dog shows repetitive in-kennel pacing, spinning, bouncing and barking, and jumping, mouthing and leash tugging out of the kennel. How is this presentation best characterised?
o: Self-handicapping behaviour typical of geriatric dogs
Neophobia secondary to aggression toward other dogs
Excessive arousal, which can increase length of stay and reduce the likelihood of adoption
e: Hyper-responsiveness, exaggerated emotionality and reduced behavioural inhibition define excessive arousal, which reduces adoptability.

q: A shelter wants auditory enrichment to reduce barking and stress in a high-arousal ward. Which stimulus is supported by published data?
o: High-tempo electronic dance music
Slow-tempo piano or violin music
Continuous white noise at 90 decibels
e: Slow-tempo classical piano or violin decreased barking, increased resting and improved heart rate variability.

q: A fearful, unsocialised dog from a hoarding case has daily behaviour modification at the ASPCA Behavior Rehabilitation Center. Which concurrent psychotropic combination is documented?
o: Acepromazine and meloxicam
Fluoxetine and gabapentin
Dexmedetomidine and phenobarbital
e: Standardised fear rehabilitation combines environmental enrichment, structured behaviour modification, and daily fluoxetine with gabapentin.

q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Dogs Playing for Life (DPFL) and Shelter Playgroup Alliance (SPA) models?
o: DPFL restricts groups to 2 to 3 dogs, whereas SPA advocates groups of 15 or more.
SPA bans basket muzzles entirely, whereas DPFL requires them for all dogs.
DPFL uses an every-dog-every-day approach with large groups (6 or more) for efficiency, whereas SPA emphasises smaller groups, strict handler ratios and choice.
e: DPFL prioritises efficiency with large groups. SPA limits group size, uses handler ratios and emphasises LIMA and dog choice.

q: A multi-site study measured post-playgroup salivary cortisol. Which group showed increased cortisol?
o: Dogs in small playgroups given treats and vocal praise
Dogs in the control shelter with no playgroups
Dogs in a small playgroup where handlers regularly used aversive tools
e: Post-playgroup cortisol rose specifically in small groups where handlers regularly used aversive tools.

q: A shelter veterinarian sets playgroup safety protocols. Which candidate-selection rule is standard?
o: Candidates are selected only after veterinary clearance, because play is not universally safe or reinforcing.
All dogs enter daily regardless of medical status, so that none is excluded.
Dogs with active respiratory disease are prioritised, since play helps them recover.
e: Veterinary clearance is mandatory. Play is species typical but not universally safe or enriching.

q: A dog voluntarily places itself in a less advantageous position and slows its movements to sustain a social interaction. Which healthy play component is this?
o: Self-handicapping
Displacement grooming
Redirected play
e: Self-handicapping is voluntarily using less advantageous strategies to keep play going.

q: Which cues are most often misinterpreted as play when they may indicate arousal or conflict, and which is a reliable play signal?
o: Barking, bouncing, forward-erect ears and tail wagging; a play bow with a distinct pause
Inhibited biting, play bows and hip thrusts; low-intensity herding with a tucked tail
Piloerection, standing over and showing teeth; mutual resting and ground sniffing
e: Handlers often mistake barking, bouncing, erect ears and tail wagging for play, although they can signal arousal or conflict. A play bow with a brief pause is a stable, reliable play invitation.

q: Two large dogs engage in intensive body contact with growling and forceful reciprocal movements, without injury or distress vocalisation. What is this, and into what does it carry the highest risk of transitioning?
o: Play wrestling, with the highest risk of transitioning into play-induced conflict and aggression
Self-handicapping, with the highest risk of transitioning into cardiovascular collapse
Low-intensity stalking, with the highest risk of transitioning into learned helplessness
e: Play wrestling is continuous reciprocal body contact without injury, and it carries the highest risk of turning into conflict or aggression.

q: A handler designs an outdoor multi-dog yard. Which configuration is recommended?
o: Multiple connected zones with separate entrance and exit pens, high fencing, two-way gates, and platforms or benches
A single tight concrete run with one one-way gate
A large open field with no structures and raw marrow bones for the dogs
e: Multi-zone yards with separate pens, escape architecture and two-way gates reduce conflict and give dogs places to retreat.

q: During a playgroup a dog repeatedly mounts a familiar play partner. How should the handler interpret this?
o: It is an irreversible sign of predatory aggression.
It can be a displacement behaviour from frustration or high motivation for a blocked behaviour.
It is a sign that the dog has achieved a cognitive map of the yard.
e: Mounting often serves as a displacement behaviour arising from arousal or frustrated motivation.

q: A resilient helper dog is used repeatedly in many consecutive sessions. What is the primary welfare concern?
o: The helper dog will lose the ability to distinguish play from aggression.
Overuse puts the helper dog at increased risk of injury, behavioural fatigue and stress.
The helper dog will develop non-social fear of other dogs.
e: Repeated use of the same helper dog increases the risk of injury, fatigue and stress, so helpers are rotated.

q: According to retrospective data, what is the average incidence of canine infectious respiratory disease complex in shelter playgroup populations?
o: Less than 0.1%
About 19%
Over 85%
e: The retrospective data show an average incidence of about 19% for canine respiratory disease, with parvovirus under 1% and distemper 0%.

q: What is the formal name for a protocol that confirms a dog's willingness to take part in a playgroup?
o: A LIMA threshold index
A stereotypic baseline count
A consent test, choice test or preference assessment
e: Consent or choice tests formally confirm an individual dog's willingness before it enters a playgroup.

q: Which restraint tool is explicitly not recommended for use within shelter playgroups?
o: Gentle Leader head collars
Properly fitted basket muzzles
6 ft (1.8 m) nylon or leather leashes
e: Gentle Leader head collars are not recommended in off-leash, multi-dog play settings.

q: Under the SPA model for a high-risk-tolerance set-up, what is the maximum recommended group size and handler ratio?
o: 12 to 15 dogs with a single handler
2 to 3 dogs, with 10 handlers per dog
4 to 6 dogs per playgroup, with 3 dogs per handler
e: SPA recommends 4 to 6 dogs and a dog-to-handler ratio of 3:1 for organisations with high risk tolerance.

q: When handlers step into the yard and begin bowing, clapping or patting the floor, dog-to-dog play decreases. Why?
o: These actions trigger auditory neophobia in the dogs.
These actions act as positive punishment for the dogs' play.
These actions invite human-dog play, competing with the dogs' motivation for dog-to-dog play.
e: Human play signals evoke human-directed play and reduce dog-to-dog play.

q: A shelter adds pre- and post-adoption counselling to its standard services. What benefit is documented?
o: A 50% reduction in operating costs
27.5% more adopted dogs than at a comparable shelter without the programme
A 16% increase in returns after adoption
e: Pre- and post-adoption counselling was associated with a 27.5% increase in successful adoptions.

q: A shelter uses the SPIDER framework for its enrichment and playgroup strategies. What do the letters stand for?
o: Stereotypy, Pacing, Impulsivity, Distress, Excitability and Reactivity
Stimulation, Perception, Ingestion, Depolarisation, Evaluation and Regulation
Setting goals, Planning, Implementation, Documentation, Evaluation and Readjustment
e: SPIDER is a programme framework: Setting goals, Planning, Implementation, Documentation, Evaluation and Readjustment.

q: When must a conflict and fight management plan be developed and communicated to staff?
o: It must be planned, prepared and shared among staff before playgroups begin.
Immediately after the first fight that causes an injury.
During the annual audit of the shelter's safety procedures.
e: Conflict plans must be in place before any playgroup starts, with input from all involved staff.

q: A dog with on-leash reactivity and barrier barking is being evaluated for playgroup entry. How should these behaviours be interpreted?
o: They are reliable predictors of aggression toward dogs off leash.
On-leash and barrier reactivity are not accurate predictors of aggression or sociability off leash.
The dog should be permanently excluded from all social enrichment.
e: On-leash and barrier reactivity do not predict off-leash sociability, so the dog may still be a suitable playgroup candidate.

q: Standard fear rehabilitation protocols focus on which four target categories?
o: Fear of sound, light, movement and temperature
Fear of cats, crates, vehicles and structures
Fear of people, handling, leashing and leash walking, and novelty
e: The four axes are fear of people, handling, leashing and walking, and novelty.

q: What is the average playgroup size across shelters, and how does group size relate to fights and injuries?
o: About 8 dogs, with no correlation between group size and the rate of fights or injuries
About 50 dogs, with an unpredictable correlation between group size and fights
About 2 dogs, with a strong positive correlation between group size and fights
e: The average is about 8 dogs, and no correlation between group size and fight or injury rates has been found.

q: A trainer argues that praise and petting should be the primary reinforcer in shelter dog training. How does this compare with published data?
o: It is correct: praise is more effective than food for shelter dogs.
It is incorrect: praise and petting were ineffective as primary reinforcers for shelter dogs, whereas food rewards were effective.
It is correct only for dogs with a history of biting.
e: Studies show that praise and petting are ineffective primary reinforcers for shelter dogs, whereas food rewards are effective.

q: A shelter records a 1% return rate for dogs that had behaviour modification. What is the general baseline return rate for dogs that did not?
o: Less than 0.5%
Over 75%
About 16%
e: Dogs that had behaviour modification had only 1% returns, compared with a general baseline of about 16%.
